top_story: Israel’s first ground push into Gaza since the ceasefire began, followed hours later by strikes on residential areas near the Bureij and Nuseirat camps, signals a rapid erosion of the truce and is again driving displacement among families who had only briefly paused flight. The renewed military pressure in Gaza coincides with lethal violence in the West Bank, where a 72-year-old Palestinian woman was killed near Jericho in an apparent settler attack, reinforcing a wider pattern of insecurity that reaches beyond formal front lines. Outside the immediate war zone, the US sentencing of a Pakistani man for a Trump assassination plot framed as revenge for Qassem Suleimani’s killing underscores how older regional grievances still animate transnational violence years later. The clearest takeaway is that localized pauses in fighting are proving too fragile to contain a conflict ecosystem that keeps spilling across geographies, actors, and civilian life.
